feedback: ACCEPT with minor notes. (1) Format: header (STATES/INITIAL_STATE/FINAL_STATES), TRANSITION_FUNCTION and REWARD_FUNCTION follow the paper format; FINAL_STATES is nonempty, u6 is declared and accepting, and every listed reward triple matches an existing transition exactly. (2) Semantic fidelity: the automaton faithfully encodes 'pick it up on the very next move after each fall'. At a fall step box_fell and holding_box are mutually exclusive, so u0->u1/u2->u3 land in an 'awaiting' state, and the ordered guards (holding_box) -> progress vs (!holding_box) -> failure resolve exactly one step later — the earliest possible evaluation, matching the immediate-pickup deadline. The recovery check correctly uses persistent holding_box since no pickup event predicate exists. Progression and failure edges from u1/u3 cover all labels, so siren_ringing/switch_toggled cannot disturb the deadline; siren, toggle and switch events are rightly absent from the spec and covered by the per-state else self-loops in every state. Progression is rewarded (+0.2), failure is explicit (-0.2), and the fall itself is unpenalized — correct, since falls are exogenous and uncontrollable. (3) Structure vs dynamics: the linear chain u0..u4 matches the environment's fall budget (the start is the first pickup, so the earliest second fall is 2 steps after the first recovery — box_fell cannot fire while still in u1, and no third fall exists, so u4 correctly omits a box_fell edge). All states are reachable; u6 is reachable via at_exit & holding_box from u2/u4, so the task is attainable; u5/u6 are absorbing sinks. (4) Reward safety: all rewards are small and bounded (total range -0.4..+1.4); the exit reward requires holding_box, which is the safe, hack-proof choice: it cannot be gamed, is unobtainable by a policy that violates the recovery obligation (u1/u3 force failure before any exit), and the only trajectory it denies (drop after recovery, exit boxless) is one the task does not reward, so the induced optimal policy is task-optimal. (5) Minor notes, non-blocking: (u0, at_exit & holding_box)->u6 is dead code — the first fall always fires by step 8 while the exit needs >=10 moves, so u0 can never see at_exit; the else edges in u1 and u3 are shadowed because the holding_box/!holding_box pair already covers all labels; u3/u4 mirror u1/u2, so a cyclic u2->u1-on-box_fall design would be 2 states more compact — the explicit chain is acceptable given the hard two-fall budget; the at_exit & holding_box guard at the terminal step is consistent with the constraint that box_fell/at_exit and switch_toggled/at_exit never co-occur, so no guard can be preempted by an impossible co-occurrence. Overall: well-formed, faithful, safe, and complete; no rewrite required.
